# E082 -- HSBC Brand Identity Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Brand**: HSBC
- **Industry**: Banking / Financial Services
- **Year**: July 2018 (Version 1.3)
- **Source file**: `509700ba950345a78c97dbdf07798f1d.pdf`
- **Pages reviewed**: 1-2, 3-5, 6-7, 12-13
- **Total pages**: 181
- **Format**: 1920x1080 presentation format

## Brand Strategy
- **Brand Purpose**: Advancing prosperity for all we serve today, tomorrow and into the future.
- **Brand Promise**: "Together we thrive" -- translated into French, Spanish, Arabic, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese.
- Brand identity positioned as the most significant evolution in the brand's history, raising the profile of the iconic hexagon logo.
- Strong governance: all work shared with Global Brand Design team for audit and quality control during transition.

## Logo
- **The Hexagon**: central brand mark, referred to as the iconic logo element.
- Masterbrand primary version plus other versions.
- Regional logos for non-English markets: Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese with custom "small usage" versions for when hexagon height is 8mm or less.
- Sub brands and legal entities with English and non-English/bilingual variants.
- Protected area and minimum size rules defined.
- Positioning rules for general use, photographic backgrounds, with brand promise, end frames, digital/display/social.
- File formats: .eps, .tiff (print), .svg, .png (digital).
- Brand architecture: Masterbrand leads every communication; framework for new propositions; comprehensive overview of brand appearance.

## Typography
- Dedicated section (Section 7): Latin and Non-Latin typefaces.
- Typographic style rules defined.
- Digital type hierarchy specified separately in the digital section.

## Color
- **Core palette** with illustration and animation examples.
- HSBC Red CMYK updated in v1.3: C0 M100 Y100 K0.
- Charts and graphs palette with specific usage rules.
- **Digital color space** (Section 5): separate treatment for apps/web, backgrounds, RAG colors, interaction language color, active navigation, binary form elements, sliders.
- Brand fragmentation addressed in color section.
- Business lines and sub-brands each have their own color palettes (Premier, Jade, Fusion).

## Graphics
- **The Nexus** (Section 8): brand graphic element with tints on flat color, usage for external and internal communications.
- "Thriving Hexagons" as a key brand device: when used, how they work, placement rules.
- Nexus focal point, clashing lines rules, legibility requirements.
- Icons (Section 6): color usage, icon characteristics, states, pictograms, pictogram/icon usage guidelines.

## Photography
- Section 9: general photography overview, choosing photography, "things we like" / "things to avoid" guidance.
- Photography integrated with Nexus usage rules.

## Applications
- Extremely comprehensive:
  - **Literature** (Section 16): A4/A5/DL brochure covers and spreads, grid system, fund brochures, newsletters, factsheets, whitepapers.
  - **Stationery** (Section 17): letterhead (A4/US), continuation sheets, compliments slips, business cards, envelopes (DL/C4/C5), folders, global cards.
  - **Digital** (Section 18): eNewsletter, email footer, layout guidance.
  - **Events** (Section 19): eInvitations, print invitations, corporate backdrops, stage dressing, merchandise.
  - **App Icon System** (Section 15): mobile app icons, core banking apps, sub-brand apps, product/utility apps, internal apps, watch app, social icons, app store best practices.
  - **Communications** (Section 13): advertising hierarchy, outdoor, print, digital, format examples.
  - **Email signature** added in v1.3.

## Tone of Voice
- Section 10: overview and pillars defined.
- Specific details not captured in text reads but section exists.

## Outliers
- **Naming system** (Section 11): comprehensive naming approach, process, background research, name generation, application/approval process, domain IP, glossary, best practices, third-party naming examples. Unusually thorough for brand guidelines.
- **App icon system** is extremely detailed -- covers core banking, sub-brand, product/utility, internal, watch, social, and app store best practices. One of the most complete app icon systems seen.
- Multilingual logo variants with custom small-usage sizes for Chinese scripts.
- Historical brand imagery (1912-1953 photos) included in introduction -- heritage emphasis.
- Version-controlled document with detailed changelog.

## Quality Score
5/5 -- Exceptionally comprehensive 181-page document covering every conceivable brand touchpoint. Detailed sections on logo architecture, color (including digital-specific), typography, naming, app icon systems, literature grids, events, and digital applications. Enterprise-grade brand governance with multilingual support and version control.
